items.headline: One CLI tool that extracts an entire site's design into files so Claude Code rebuilds the UI exactly
items.excerpt: A Thai-language walkthrough of a CLI that scrapes a live site's design language (tokens, type scale, spacing, components) into files an agent can read, so Claude Code reproduces the UI pixel-faithfully instead of guessing.

items.headline: Claude Code vs Codex vs Hermes: Choosing the Right AI Agent Harness
items.excerpt: Argues the harness around a model — how it plans, reads context and applies edits — matters more than the model itself, and compares Claude Code, Codex and Hermes for teams shipping UI.

items.headline: Build with OpenAI Agents API on Vercel
items.excerpt: Vercel adds a path to deploy OpenAI Agents API apps with Next.js, Functions, Queues and Sandbox — isolated, persistent execution for agent-built interfaces and prototypes.

items.headline: GitHub Copilot is now available in the AI SDK harness layer
items.excerpt: Copilot now runs through Vercel's AI SDK harness via @ai-sdk/harness-github-copilot, using the same HarnessAgent interface as other agents — one swap-in interface for design-to-code pipelines.

items.headline: ChatGPT Images 2.5: What's New and How It Actually Performs
items.excerpt: Hands-on test of OpenAI's ChatGPT Images 2.5: sketch-to-image, stronger identity matching and multi-step edits. Details where it holds up for real design work and where it still breaks.

items.headline: Why is the internet so upset about NVIDIA's DLSS 5?
items.excerpt: NVIDIA calls DLSS 5 the biggest graphics breakthrough since ray tracing; critics call it an AI slop filter. A breakdown of what the generative frame pipeline actually does to authored visuals.

items.headline: SuperSplat Editor 3.0 is a huge performance update
items.excerpt: PlayCanvas' free browser tool for viewing and editing 3D Gaussian splats now handles tens of millions of Gaussians smoothly, making scanned-reality assets practical in design and visualization pipelines.

items.headline: Can you spot all the clues that prove this AI 'photo' isn't real?
items.excerpt: A forensic read of a viral AI image that fools most viewers at a glance, cataloguing the lighting and composition tells designers can train themselves to catch.

items.headline: The real reason everyone hates the viral AI food slop images
items.excerpt: "We've always made food look better than it is. So why does it feel different when AI does it?" Slava Polonski unpacks the trust mechanics behind the backlash to AI food imagery — and what it means for brand and visual design.

items.headline: Five eras of UX design and the lessons to keep in the AI era
items.excerpt: Sixty years of UX compressed into one horizon line: human factors has reinvented itself every decade since Bell Labs, and the oldest lessons are the ones pointing the way forward as AI resets the interface.

items.headline: Your first draft now has a log
items.excerpt: Workplace surveillance has reached the thought before the thought: every prompt and revision in an AI tool leaves a record. A hard look at what logged creative process means for designers and the products they build.

items.headline: ChatGPT Images 2.5 and Astra: Automate a Full Design Workflow
items.excerpt: Chains ChatGPT Images 2.5 with GPT-5 Astra across Canva, Dropbox and a print service so a single prompt runs end-to-end to a finished, print-ready poster.

items.headline: Introducing the Agents API
items.excerpt: OpenAI ships a managed Agents API powered by the Codex harness, with orchestration, long-running sessions and tool use — the plumbing behind agents that can run a design or content workflow unattended.

items.headline: Build more natural voice experiences with GPT-Live-1 in the API
items.excerpt: GPT-Live-1 brings full-duplex voice conversation to the API with stronger instruction following, custom voices and telephony support — new raw material for voice-first interface design.

items.headline: Vibe coding is Topgolf. Production is Torrey Pines.
items.excerpt: Vibe coding makes creation feel effortless; shipping it demands another level of discipline. A blueprint for keeping prompt-driven prototyping's energy while adding the guardrails production needs.

items.headline: How to get started with Meta's new AI agent, Muse
items.excerpt: After days of testing Meta's Muse agent, Engadget finds almost no learning curve — a look at how the assistant handles creative and everyday tasks in Meta's apps.

items.headline: Elon Musk's daughter's Tesla-trolling fashion advert is as cinematic as Star Wars
items.excerpt: Desigual's campaign casts Vivian Wilson opposite a humanoid robot in a sci-fi spot with several layers of trolling — a case study in how brands are staging the human-versus-machine narrative.

items.headline: Show Stop Proof Before Approving an Agent Retry
items.excerpt: A retry button looked harmless in Friday critique — until an agent had rewritten onboarding consent. A concrete interaction pattern for showing evidence of what an agent stopped before a designer approves another run.

items.headline: AI-generated websites are the Word Art era all over again
items.excerpt: Remember Word Art on every 90s school flyer? The argument that prompt-built sites are repeating the same cycle — new power, no constraints — and what design systems must supply to break it.

items.headline: Skild AI Taps NVIDIA Physical AI to Teach Robots New Tasks From a Single Video
items.excerpt: Skild AI's S1 robot foundation model learns a new task from one demonstration video, using NVIDIA synthetic data, training and simulation — collapsing the prototype loop for anyone designing physical products and robots.

items.headline: Morpholio launches Trace for Business for enterprise users
items.excerpt: The AI-assisted sketching and drawing app used by architects and industrial designers gets an enterprise tier with centralized licensing, SSO and IT management through the Vectorworks portal.

items.headline: My Actual AI Stack Right Now
items.excerpt: A working designer walks through the exact AI tools he uses to design, code, edit video and run an agency — not predictions, the current stack and where each tool stops being useful.

items.headline: I Built A Tool To Detect AI Slop (You Can Have It)
items.excerpt: AI video has gotten hard to spot, so Matt Wolfe builds and open-sources a detector — a hands-on look at which artifacts still betray generated footage.

items.headline: I Never Thought I'd See This Happen
items.excerpt: Karoly Zsolnai-Feher covers an AI system contributing to a Navier-Stokes result — the fluid math that underpins simulation and VFX work designers rely on.
